argument.statement: ECT can be lifesaving for people with severe mental illness who have not responded to other treatments, and patient stories can dispel myths and misinformation surrounding it.

book.rationale: The book focuses primarily on the medical treatment of electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) and its effects on mental health, positioning it firmly within Medicine & Public Health, while also relating to the psychological experiences of individuals undergoing treatment.
book.summary: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) can be a lifesaving treatment for people with severe mental illness that have not responded to other treatments. Yet, it remains one of the most controversial treatments in psychiatry. This book is a collection of stories written by people who have received ECT, or by their friends and family. They provide open and detailed accounts of their experiences of severe mental illness and their journeys through ECT, including any side effects of the treatment. The outcomes range from quick recoveries to relapses and repeated courses of therapy. These stories will highlight the potential life changing benefits this treatment can have and dispel some of the myths and misinformation that surround this treatment. This book will be a useful resource for anyone looking for further information about ECT and for those who want to learn about the experiences of people who have severe depression, including psychosis.
